turns.content: My wedding is six weeks away. My closest friend Rohan is supposed to be in my haldi and give a toast — he's been my guy since first year of college. But every time I bring up his travel from Bangalore he just says "let's see, I'll definitely try." Should I just book his flight myself and be done with it?

That's a tough spot. On one hand, you want Rohan there for your big day, and it'd be awesome to have him involved in the haldi ceremony. On the other hand, booking his flight without checking with him might come across as a bit presumptuous.

Maybe instead of booking the flight directly, you could have a more straightforward conversation with him? Ask him straight out if he's planning to come and if there's anything holding him back. That way, you can get a clearer idea of where he stands and avoid any potential misunderstandings.

I checked, flights are like nine thousand return. Not crazy. He switched jobs a couple of months back, some startup. And lately his replies are two words where he used to send voice notes. I'm telling myself he's busy but it's been weeks of this.

It sounds like Rohan's going through a lot right now with the job change. That can be super stressful and all-consuming. The change in his communication style is also pretty noticeable - going from voice notes to just two-word replies is a big shift.

It's possible that he's just really overwhelmed and not meaning to be distant, but it's still worrying when someone you care about starts pulling away like that. You might want to try having a more casual, low-pressure conversation with him, just to check in and see how he's doing. Ask him how the new job is going, and if there's anything on his mind that he wants to talk about. That might give you a better sense of what's going on and whether he's still on board with coming to your wedding.

Honestly it's starting to hurt now. If he actually cared he would have just said yes on day one, no? I'm thinking I should just call him tonight and ask him straight — "bro, are you coming or not, yes or no." At least I'll know where I stand.

Yeah, it's starting to hurt, and that's totally valid. It's natural to feel that way when someone you care about isn't being as clear or responsive as you'd like.

Calling him tonight and asking straight out might be a good idea. Being direct can help clear the air and give you a sense of closure, one way or the other. Just be prepared for any response - he might say yes, no, or something in between. Either way, you'll have a better idea of what's going on and can plan accordingly.

It's also okay if he says no, and it's not the end of the world. You've got a lot of other loved ones coming to celebrate with you, and that's what matters most.

My fiancée says I'm overthinking and he's probably just swamped. But this is the same guy who took an overnight bus to be at my sister's wedding in 2019. Something has changed and I can't figure out what, and I hate that I'm angry at him two weeks before my haldi.

Your fiancée's trying to offer a different perspective, and that's helpful. But you're right, too - Rohan's past behavior does suggest that he's someone who makes an effort to be there for you. So, it's natural that you're wondering what's changed.

It's not just about being angry; it's about feeling a bit hurt and confused that someone who's been so important to you isn't being as clear or responsive as you'd expect. It's okay to acknowledge those feelings, and it's good that you're recognizing them.

Having that conversation with Rohan might help you understand what's going on, and maybe even clear the air. Even if he says he's not coming, at least you'll know where you stand and can move forward.
